name: close-then-restore-tab
description: Measurement for IDC_CLOSE_TAB and IDC_RESTORE_TAB. Starts on a space WITH a restored tab (so no palette auto-opens), presses Cmd+W to close it - which leaves the window TABLESS - then Cmd+Shift+T on that now-tabless window, which is exactly the condition under test. Both commands reach AtriumBrowserWindow::ExecuteCommand's catch-all with no intercept, and both are routed through CommandTarget to the VISIBLE browser, so if that browser is tabless the no-selected-tab early return should swallow the restore the way it swallowed IDC_EXIT and IDC_CLOSE_WINDOW. The vlog assertion covers the close only: 'tab added' cannot be asserted here because startup emits it too, so whether the restore fired is read off the log's ordering by hand this round.

actions.note: let the space and its restored tab render; no palette expected
make Atrium frontmost before any synthetic chord
one window, one tab, no palette
IDC_CLOSE_TAB on a window that HAS a tab - expected to work, and it is what makes the window tabless for the next step
let the tab close and the sidebar update
evidence of what the window looks like with its only tab gone
IDC_RESTORE_TAB on the now-TABLESS window - the measurement
let any restored tab load and reach the sidebar
evidence of whether the tab came back

assertions.label: tab-closed
assertions.note: proves Cmd+W actually took - startup never closes a tab, so this line can only come from it. Without it the restore step would be measuring nothing

assertions.label: tab-restored
assertions.note: The earlier guard: the restored tab. The id is deliberate rather than [0-9]+ - this fixture restores exactly ONE tab at startup, which takes id 1, so id 2 can only be the Cmd+Shift+T restore. A generic pattern would match the startup tab and pass vacuously, which is precisely how a guard like that stays green over a live bug. Measured: absent before the IDC_RESTORE_TAB intercept, present after
